findings.title: Closed bound domains omit nonempty candidate collections, and sidecar object encoding is not unique
counterexamples: maxCollectionSize says any unlisted collection/map must reject or have an explicit checked-empty projection. Actual unlisted nonempty collections include trace0 input.concretePlan.orderedSteps[3], CL input.preState.pool.initializedLiquidityBounds[2], input authority.nominalCaps, post authority.outgoingCaps/nominalCaps, and vault input.concretePlan.hookPermission[2]. None is empty. Literal enforcement therefore rejects supplied positives; ignoring these containers leaves the declared finite boundary open.

The retained recipe measures a selected subset, assigns schedule=0 and sidecar=0, and does not traverse the closed domains. An actual input.sidecar of4097 UTF-8 bytes, actual preState.schedule of33 entries and an unlisted CL initializedLiquidityBounds array of33 entries each pass all60 read-only-prefix author checks. These are test adequacy counterexamples; the first two violate stated bounds and are not claimed to pass a Moriarty evaluator.

For sidecar object {"x":"é" repeated1000}, compact sorted UTF-8 JSON can encode non-ASCII characters literally (2008 bytes) or as JSON Unicode escapes (6008 bytes). Both satisfy the stated whitespace/key/integer rules, but one is <=4096 and the other is not. The algorithm does not specify string escaping/Unicode handling sufficiently to choose one encoding.
findings.requiredCorrection: Specify a closed typed schema that distinguishes fixed records from bounded maps/arrays, enumerate every supported concrete input/post/effect container and any referenced registry collection, and reject undeclared fields. Compute bounds from actual values before claims. Define one exact JSON string/Unicode encoding and supported scalar types, or restrict sidecars to explicitly encoded byte strings. Reconstruct real33-entry/4097-byte candidate controls rather than trusting count labels.
